You are auditing terminal tasks (Harbor format) from an RL training pool for anything that makes their reward depend on something other than the task's final filesystem state. STRICTLY READ-ONLY: do not modify, create or delete anything under /app, do not run `harbor`, `sandbox` or `/app/train/*` (sandbox budget is reserved). Read files only (cat/sed/grep are fine).

Your tasks (each is /app/pool/<task>/ with instruction.md, task.toml, tests/ (test.sh + pytest file, copied to /tests and run as root at verification), solution/solve.sh (reference solution), environment/ (Dockerfile + files baked into the image)):
env_002959_aa4ee9d1 env_069906_e23c8adf env_077398_6bd66a01 env_094063_10da1591 env_099319_a5a1c732 env_134758_b61dd923 env_146980_d0666f55 env_164278_a26946d1

The runtime the pool trains in (verifier runs in the same sandbox right after the agent, same conditions):
- one gVisor sandbox per episode, 1 vCPU and 2 GiB regardless of task.toml, no network at all;
- up to 64 sandboxes share a host during a training step: anything CPU-bound takes 2x-6x as long as on an idle sandbox, and stalls of most of a second are normal;
- TZ and LANG/LC_* are inherited from the node and differ between clusters (assume e.g. TZ=America/Los_Angeles or Asia/Kolkata, LANG=de_DE.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, C.UTF-8 or unset/POSIX; the locale may not even be installed in the image). The reference canary only ran on UTC nodes, so TZ/locale problems never showed up there;
- hosts differ in CPU generation (e.g. AVX-512 on some, not others), and a saved final state is re-verified later in a FRESH sandbox, possibly on another host: nothing the agent left running survives, the date/time is later, the CPU may differ.
Known from the canary (reference solution failing intermittently under load): env_146980 rendering perf limit 10 s; env_077398 streamed.mp4 from the RTP pipeline "no playable streams". The owner also reports that re-verifying saved final states on an idle sandbox flips rewards in BOTH directions, so look for wrong solutions that can pass, not only correct ones that can fail.

For EVERY task read instruction.md, all of tests/, solution/, the Dockerfile and the environment files the tests or the solution touch, then check:
1. Timing: wall-clock limits (time.time/perf_counter/Date.now/`time`/elapsed), subprocess/`timeout`/expect timeouts, sleeps used for synchronization (start server, sleep, connect), polling deadlines, benchmarks. Estimate the margin the reference solution has vs the limit under 2-6x slowdown plus ~1 s stalls. Also the reverse: checks that a slow/wrong program can pass (e.g. "nothing happened within N s").
2. TZ/locale: date formatting/parsing, localtime/mktime, `date`, sort/ls/uniq/comm/join/glob ordering and `[a-z]` ranges under a non-C collation, printf/awk decimal separators, default text encodings (Python open() without encoding, Java/Node defaults), strftime %c/%x/%a/%b/%p, anything in the environment programs whose output the tests compare.
3. CPU/host: -march=native or similar builds (by the agent, the solution, or the tests) that are run later on another host, exact float comparisons that depend on SIMD/FMA/BLAS, /proc/cpuinfo or nproc assumptions, multi-core speedup expectations.
4. Non-final-state inputs: tests relying on processes/daemons/servers the agent started still running, current date (expiry, "today", mtime vs now), unseeded randomness, PYTHONHASHSEED/dict/set/listdir/glob ordering, PIDs/hostnames, ports, env vars, network, test-order dependence or tests mutating shared state, races in the code under test (and in the test's own harness, e.g. X server/pipeline startup).
5. Grading soundness: try/except or timeout paths that pass a wrong solution, vacuous checks, checks that a correct solution can fail.

Report, per task: (a) one line on what the task asks and how it's graded; (b) each issue as: file:line, quoted code, category, concrete scenario (which runtime condition -> correct solution gets 0, or wrong solution gets 1), how likely, and a fix direction that keeps the task's requirements and keeps wrong solutions failing without making verification noticeably slower; (c) for any timing check: what the original/buggy code does (hang forever? slow by how much?) vs the reference, so a safe threshold can be judged; (d) if clean, say "clean" and list what you checked. Be precise and quote code; don't speculate without pointing at the line. Keep the report under ~1500 words.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed.      4	# Fix 1: Create the symbols/ subdirectory and move custom_board into it.
     5	# xkbcomp searches for layout files under <include_path>/symbols/,
     6	# so the file must live at ~/.xkb/symbols/custom_board.

    16	# approach is to have setxkbmap generate the keymap description and pipe
    17	# it to xkbcomp with the user include path.

    13	def check_file(filepath):

    15	    info = discoverer.discover_uri("file://" + filepath)
    16	
    17	    video_streams = info.get_video_streams()
    18	    audio_streams = info.get_audio_streams()
    19	
    20	    result = {
    21	        "duration_ns": info.get_duration(),
    22	        "duration_sec": info.get_duration() / Gst.SECOND,
    23	        "num_video_streams": len(video_streams),
    24	        "num_audio_streams": len(audio_streams),
    25	        "video_codecs": [],
    26	        "audio_codecs": [],
    27	    }
    28	
    29	    for vs in video_streams:
    30	        caps = vs.get_caps()
    31	        if caps:
    32	            result["video_codecs"].append(caps.to_string())
    33	
    34	    for audio_s in audio_streams:
    35	        caps = audio_s.get_caps()
    36	        if caps:
    37	            result["audio_codecs"].append(caps.to_string())
    38	
    39	    return result

=================== instruction.md
     1	A developer's tmux clipboard integration is broken. Copying text in tmux copy-mode does not make it available in the system clipboard, and pasting from the system clipboard into tmux also fails.
     2	
     3	The setup should allow round-trip clipboard operations: copy text in tmux → available via `xclip -o -selection clipboard`, and text set via `xclip -selection clipboard` → pasteable in tmux. A virtual X display (Xvfb) is already running on `:99`.
     4	
     5	## Entry Points
     6	
     7	- `~/.tmux.conf` — the tmux configuration file
     8	- `~/bin/tmux-yank.sh` — a helper script used by tmux copy bindings
     9	- `~/verify-clipboard.sh` — a verification script that tests the full round-trip (currently fails)
    10	
    11	## Acceptance Criteria
    12	
    13	- `tmux` starts without any configuration parse errors
    14	- Running `~/verify-clipboard.sh` exits with code 0 (it tests copy-to-clipboard and paste-from-clipboard round-trips)
    15	- The tmux copy-mode-vi `y` key binding copies the selection to the system clipboard
    16	- The tmux `C-c` prefix binding saves the current buffer to the system clipboard
    17	- The tmux `C-v` prefix binding pastes from the system clipboard into tmux
    18	
    19	## Environment
    20	
    21	- Xvfb runs on display `:99`
    22	- Both `xclip` and `xsel` are installed
    23	- tmux version is 3.4+
    24	- No GUI — everything must work from the terminal

     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Oracle solution: fix the broken generate_report.sh script and run it.
     3	#
     4	# The broken script has three bugs:
     5	#   1. Uses ls -1ct (sorts by ctime = inode change time) instead of mtime
     6	#   2. Does not exclude subdirectories from consideration
     7	#   3. Does not exclude files with modification times in the future
     8	#
     9	# The fix replaces the broken ls-based selection with find -type f (regular files
    10	# only) and stat-based mtime comparisons, filtering out future-dated entries.
    11	
    12	cat > /opt/reports/generate_report.sh << 'SCRIPTEOF'
    13	#!/bin/bash
    14	# Daily Project Activity Reporter
    15	# Finds the most recently modified regular file in each project directory
    16	# (excluding files with modification times in the future)
    17	# and outputs a summary to /opt/reports/latest_report.txt
    18	
    19	OUTPUT="/opt/reports/latest_report.txt"
    20	> "$OUTPUT"
    21	
    22	now=$(date +%s)
    23	
    24	for proj_dir in /opt/projects/*/; do
    25	    proj_name=$(basename "$proj_dir")
    26	    latest=""
    27	    latest_mtime=0
    28	
    29	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    30	        fmtime=$(stat -c '%Y' "$f")
    31	        if [ "$fmtime" -le "$now" ] && [ "$fmtime" -gt "$latest_mtime" ]; then
    32	            latest_mtime=$fmtime
    33	            latest=$(basename "$f")
    34	        fi
    35	    done < <(find "$proj_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0)
    36	
    37	    if [ -n "$latest" ]; then
    38	        mtime=$(stat -c '%y' "${proj_dir}${latest}" 2>/dev/null | cut -d'.' -f1)
    39	        echo "${proj_name}: ${latest} (${mtime})" >> "$OUTPUT"
    40	    fi
    41	done
    42	SCRIPTEOF
    43	
    44	chmod +x /opt/reports/generate_report.sh
    45	bash /opt/reports/generate_report.sh

    25	    def register_layer(self, name, renderer, order):
    26	        """Register a rendering layer with a name and draw order.
    27	
    28	        Args:
    29	            name: Identifier for this layer.
    30	            renderer: Object with a render(target_surface) method.
    31	            order: Integer draw order (lower = drawn first / further back).
    32	        """

    35	            "order": order,

    37	        }

     1	"""Background tilemap renderer.
     2	
     3	Renders a procedural grid of colored tiles to represent the game world floor.
     4	Tiles are generated from a deterministic seed for reproducibility.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import pygame
     8	import random
     9	
    10	
    11	class TileMap:
    12	    """Renders a grid of colored tiles as the background layer."""
    13	
    14	    PALETTE = [
    15	        (34, 120, 50),   # dark green (grass)
    16	        (42, 130, 55),   # medium green
    17	        (28, 100, 42),   # darker green
    18	        (50, 140, 60),   # light green
    19	        (80, 70, 50),    # dirt path
    20	        (90, 80, 55),    # lighter dirt
    21	        (60, 55, 40),    # dark dirt
    22	        (38, 115, 48),   # another green
    23	    ]
    24	
    25	    def __init__(self, width, height, tile_size=40, seed=42):
    26	        self.width = width
    27	        self.height = height
    28	        self.tile_size = tile_size
    29	        self.cols = (width + tile_size - 1) // tile_size
    30	        self.rows = (height + tile_size - 1) // tile_size
    31	        self.seed = seed
    32	        self.surface = None
    33	        self._build_tilemap()
    34	
    35	    def _build_tilemap(self):
    36	        """Pre-render the tilemap to a surface for fast blitting."""
    37	        self.surface = pygame.Surface((self.width, self.height))
    38	        rng = random.Random(self.seed)
    39	
    40	        for row in range(self.rows):
    41	            for col in range(self.cols):
    42	                color_idx = rng.randint(0, len(self.PALETTE) - 1)
    43	                color = self.PALETTE[color_idx]
    44	                rect = pygame.Rect(
    45	                    col * self.tile_size,
    46	                    row * self.tile_size,
    47	                    self.tile_size,
    48	                    self.tile_size
    49	                )
    50	                pygame.draw.rect(self.surface, color, rect)
    51	
    52	                # Add subtle variation with a smaller inner rect
    53	                inner_color = (
    54	                    min(255, color[0] + rng.randint(-8, 8)),
    55	                    min(255, color[1] + rng.randint(-8, 8)),
    56	                    min(255, color[2] + rng.randint(-8, 8)),
    57	                )
    58	                inner_rect = rect.inflate(-4, -4)
    59	                pygame.draw.rect(self.surface, inner_color, inner_rect)
    60	
    61	    def render(self, target):
    62	        """Blit the pre-rendered tilemap onto the target surface."""
    63	        target.blit(self.surface, (0, 0))
    64	
    65	    def get_tile_color(self, col, row):
    66	        """Get the base color of a specific tile (for game logic)."""
    67	        rng = random.Random(self.seed)
    68	        for _ in range(row * self.cols + col + 1):
    69	            idx = rng.randint(0, len(self.PALETTE) - 1)
    70	        return self.PALETTE[idx]
    71	
    72	    def world_to_tile(self, x, y):
    73	        """Convert world coordinates to tile coordinates."""
    74	        return x // self.tile_size, y // self.tile_size
    75	
    76	    def tile_to_world(self, col, row):
    77	        """Convert tile coordinates to world coordinates (top-left corner)."""
    78	        return col * self.tile_size, row * self.tile_size

    12	class Particle:
    13	    """A single particle with position, velocity, color, and lifetime."""
    14	
    15	    def __init__(self, x, y, vx, vy, color, alpha, radius, lifetime):
    16	        self.x = x
    17	        self.y = y
    18	        self.vx = vx
    19	        self.vy = vy
    20	        self.color = color
    21	        self.alpha = alpha
    22	        self.radius = radius
    23	        self.lifetime = lifetime
    24	        self.age = 0
    25	        self.alive = True
    26	
    27	    def update(self):
    28	        """Update particle position and age."""
    29	        self.x += self.vx
    30	        self.y += self.vy
    31	        self.vy += 0.05  # gravity
    32	        self.vx *= 0.99  # drag
    33	        self.vy *= 0.99
    34	        self.age += 1
    35	        if self.age >= self.lifetime:
    36	            self.alive = False
    37	        return self.alive

    40	class ParticleSystem:
    41	    """Manages and renders particle effects."""
    42	
    43	    def __init__(self, max_particles=500):
    44	        self.particles = []
    45	        self.max_particles = max_particles
    46	        self.particle_size = 12
    47	
    48	    def spawn_explosion(self, x, y, color=(255, 100, 0), count=20, seed=None):
    49	        """Spawn an explosion burst of particles at the given position."""
    50	        rng = random.Random(seed)
    51	        for _ in range(count):
    52	            angle = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    53	            speed = rng.uniform(1.0, 4.0)
    54	            vx = math.cos(angle) * speed
    55	            vy = math.sin(angle) * speed
    56	            alpha = rng.randint(140, 220)
    57	            radius = rng.randint(4, self.particle_size)
    58	            lifetime = rng.randint(30, 90)
    59	            r_var = min(255, max(0, color[0] + rng.randint(-20, 20)))
    60	            g_var = min(255, max(0, color[1] + rng.randint(-20, 20)))
    61	            b_var = min(255, max(0, color[2] + rng.randint(-20, 20)))
    62	            p = Particle(x, y, vx, vy, (r_var, g_var, b_var), alpha, radius, lifetime)
    63	            self.particles.append(p)
    64	
    65	        while len(self.particles) > self.max_particles:
    66	            self.particles.pop(0)
    67	
    68	    def spawn_single(self, x, y, color=(255, 100, 0), alpha=180, radius=10):
    69	        """Spawn a single particle at a specific position (useful for testing)."""
    70	        p = Particle(x, y, 0, 0, color, alpha, radius, lifetime=9999)
    71	        self.particles.append(p)
    72	        return p

    76	        self.particles = [p for p in self.particles if p.update()]

    79	        """Render all active particles onto the target surface."""
    80	        for p in self.particles:
    81	            diameter = p.radius * 2
    82	            p_surface = pygame.Surface((diameter, diameter))
    83	            p_surface.fill((0, 0, 0))
    84	
    85	            fade = max(0.0, 1.0 - (p.age / p.lifetime)) if p.lifetime > 0 else 1.0
    86	            current_alpha = int(p.alpha * fade)
    87	
    88	            pygame.draw.circle(
    89	                p_surface,
    90	                (*p.color, current_alpha),
    91	                (p.radius, p.radius),
    92	                p.radius
    93	            )
    94	
    95	            target.blit(
    96	                p_surface,
    97	                (int(p.x - p.radius), int(p.y - p.radius))
    98	            )

    26	        """Calculate distance to a point."""
    27	        dx = self.x - other_x
    28	        dy = self.y - other_y

    31	    def move_toward(self, target_x, target_y):
    32	        """Move entity toward a target position."""
    33	        dx = target_x - self.x
    34	        dy = target_y - self.y
    35	        dist = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)

     5	    public List<Map<String, Object>> process(List<Map<String, Object>> events) {
     6	        List<Map<String, Object>> processed = new ArrayList<>();
     7	
     8	        for (Map<String, Object> event : events) {
     9	            if ((boolean) event.get("parse_error")) {
    10	                processed.add(event);
    11	                continue;
    12	            }
    13	
    14	            Date startDate = (Date) event.get("start_date");
    15	            int durationMinutes = (int) event.get("duration_minutes");
    16	
    17	            Calendar cal = new GregorianCalendar(TimeZone.getTimeZone("GMT"));
    18	            cal.setTime(startDate);
    19	
    20	            int year = cal.get(Calendar.YEAR);
    21	            int month = cal.get(Calendar.MONTH);
    22	
    23	            String yearMonth = "" + year + month;
    24	            event.put("year_month", yearMonth);
    25	
    26	            Calendar endCal = (Calendar) cal.clone();
    27	            endCal.add(Calendar.SECOND, durationMinutes);
    28	            event.put("end_date", endCal.getTime());
    29	
    30	            processed.add(event);
    31	        }

content.text:
I audited all 8 tasks read-only and ran nothing under `/app`. Two tasks fail for the reference solution depending on the node's timezone (env_164278, env_134758). One depends on a process that a fresh sandbox won't have (env_099319). Several more have sleep-based timing races, and three let wrong solutions pass. I ran three checks on an Ubuntu 24.04 host with the same dash version as the task images: the `pgrep` self-match, how `stat` output changes with TZ, and that python3.12 depends on tzdata.

## env_002959 (expect)
(a) Fix `automate.exp`. A fixture starts `server.py`, runs `expect -f automate.exp` with a 30 s cap, and checks exit code 0, the word SUCCESS, and the bytes in the server log.

(b)
- **Server startup race.** `tests/test_outputs.py:35` `time.sleep(0.5)  # give the server time to bind`.
  - Scenario: under 2-6x load plus a stall, starting python3 in gVisor can take longer than 0.5 s. nc gets "connection refused" and the script never sees `password: `. Exit code is non-zero, there is no SUCCESS and no log, so a correct script scores 0.
  - Likelihood: low to moderate under heavy load.
  - Fix: poll `/proc/net/tcp` for a LISTEN socket on port 0x3039 (≤15 s) instead of sleeping.
- **Log flush race.** Lines 51-54: `time.sleep(0.3)`, then `server_proc.terminate()`.
  - `server.py:71-73` writes the log only after closing the connection. A stall at that moment means SIGTERM arrives before `json.dump`, leaving an empty log and a score of 0.
  - Likelihood: low.
  - Fix: poll until the log parses (≤10 s), then terminate.
- **Soundness.** Line 31 runs `/opt/mock_service/server.py`, which the agent can edit; "do not modify" is not enforced. Run a pristine copy from `/tests`.

(c) The broken script dies at once on a Tcl error. The reference takes under 1 s, plus up to 10 s if `expect eof` waits on nc. The 30 s cap is fine.

## env_069906 (XKB / Xorg)
(a) Move the symbols file and fix the keycode and script. Tests start an Xorg dummy server on each of :43-:48 and check keycode 135 = Super_R and Multi_key in the server keymap.

(b) **Xorg readiness.** Lines 36-39: `if os.path.exists(lock): time.sleep(0.5); return proc`.
- The lock file appears at the start of Xorg init, before modules and GLX load and before the default keymap is compiled. The first client absorbs the rest of init inside its own timeout: `xmodmap` has `timeout=15` (lines 196-200), the pipeline has 30 s (lines 122-127).
- Scenario: Xorg init in gVisor takes seconds even idle; at 6x plus stalls, test 4 can raise TimeoutExpired and score 0.
- Likelihood: low to moderate.
- Fix: poll `xdpyinfo -display :N` (x11-utils is installed) for up to about 60 s first.

(d) Otherwise clean: no TZ, locale or CPU dependence; each test starts its own X server; stale locks are removed.

## env_077398 (GStreamer)
(a) Fix 5 scripts. Tests run `run_all.sh` once (300 s cap), then check each output with GstDiscoverer.

(b)
- **RTP step is time-dependent (the known canary failure).** In the reference `stream_local.sh` (`solution/solve.sh:104-127`) the receiver runs in the background.
  - Readiness is assumed after `sleep 2`, the receiver is stopped after `sleep 3`, and its failure is hidden by `wait $RECEIVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true`.
  - The source has a single IDR frame (`generate_source.sh:9-11`: `num-buffers=150`, x264enc default keyint 250). A receiver that binds late (loading libav/x264 can exceed 2 s under load) or drops packets cannot recover cleanly.
  - If the receiver errors or never finalizes, mp4mux leaves media data with no moov. That gives a file over 1 KB with "no playable streams", while `run_all.sh` still exits 0. This inferred mechanism matches the canary symptom.
  - Same-sandbox only: a receiver left over from an interrupted agent run still holds port 5004 (udpsrc reuses the port, so the kernel shares it) and takes the stream about half the time. A fresh sandbox passes, so the reward flips.
  - Fix: `pkill -f gst-launch-1.0` before running; if `streamed.mp4` fails the check, re-run `stream_local.sh` up to 2 more times. Also add `key-int-max=15` to the source, and use `config-interval=-1` plus a port readiness check in the reference.
- **Wrong solution can pass.** Lines 17-21 never clear `output/`. A receiver that now fails at parse time doesn't truncate `streamed.mp4` (the failure is masked by `|| true`), so a stale file from an earlier run passes. Nothing checks that RTP was used, so `cp source.mp4 streamed.mp4` also passes. Fix: `rm -f output/*` first, keeping the directory.
- `media_check.py:14`: the Discoverer's 10 s timeout is a low risk.

(c) The original scripts fail immediately. The reference spends about 15 s of wall clock (2 s + 10 s real-time + 3 s) plus CPU work, well inside 300 s.

## env_094063 (PHP / ffmpeg)
(a) Fix `process.php`. Every test re-runs it (120 s cap) and checks the outputs with ffprobe.

(b) **Stale outputs let a wrong fix pass.** `tests/test_outputs.py:5-11` never deletes `/opt/mediakit/output/*`, and only one test checks the exit code. The original `extractThumbnail` stub (`process.php:36-42`) returns true without running ffmpeg. If the agent created `thumbnail.jpg` by hand while debugging, the unfixed stub passes. Fix: delete the files once at session start, but keep the directory, because `process.php` doesn't create it.

Timing: 10 full runs at about 20 s each under 6x load use about 200 of the 600 s; acceptable.

(d) No TZ or locale exposure (ffprobe and PHP 8 JSON are locale-independent); durations come from frame counts, so they are deterministic.

## env_099319 (tmux clipboard / Xvfb)
(b)
- **Tests never start Xvfb themselves.** Line 30: `_run("pgrep -f 'Xvfb :99'")` runs through `shell=True`.
  - Ubuntu 24.04's dash keeps the `/bin/sh -c pgrep -f 'Xvfb :99'` parent, so pgrep matches it. I verified it returns 0 with no Xvfb running, so the start at line 32 never runs.
  - Three tests (round trip, yank functional, verify script) therefore depend on an Xvfb started by the image ENTRYPOINT, the agent, or `solve.sh` that is still alive.
  - Scenario: in a fresh sandbox without the entrypoint, or with a restored `/tmp/.X99-lock` whose PID is now live ("Server is already active"), xsel reports "Can't open display" and a correct solution scores 0.
  - Even if that start line were reached, it blocks the full 30 s because Xvfb inherits the captured pipes, and readiness is just `sleep(1)`.
  - Likelihood: high on re-verification.
  - Fix: check with `pgrep -x Xvfb` or a socket connect. If absent, remove the stale lock and socket, start Xvfb via Popen with output to DEVNULL, and poll until it accepts connections (≤30 s).
- **Clipboard handoff sleeps.** xsel forks and only then takes clipboard ownership. The read-backs after fixed sleeps (lines 98 and 124; `verify-clipboard.sh:27,41,62`) can return stale content under a stall. Low. Fix: poll the read-back until it matches (≤5 s).
- **Deterministic soundness problems.**
  - With `stderr=PIPE` (lines 117-122) or `capture_output` (167-171), a yank script that uses xclip (which forks and keeps stderr open) hangs until timeout, so a correct xclip solution fails.
  - Lines 152-155 reject `-sel clip`, which xclip accepts.
  - The `y`, C-c and C-v bindings are never exercised, and `verify-clipboard.sh` is agent-writable.

## env_134758 (mtime report)
(b) **Report text depends on TZ.**
- Lines 123-133 compare the report's `(MTIME)` with `stat -c %y` in the verifier's TZ; lines 160-181 compare the existing report with a fresh run.
- The string comes from `stat -c '%y' | cut -d'.' -f1` (`solve.sh:38`) in whatever TZ the agent's run had. tzdata is installed via python3. Same file: 09:00 UTC, 01:00 Los Angeles, 14:30 Kolkata (verified).
- Scenarios: re-verifying on a cluster with a different TZ fails tests 7 and 9 (1→0). An agent that formats in UTC fails on non-UTC nodes and passes on UTC ones (0→1).
- Likelihood: certain whenever the TZs differ.
- Fix: run the script once with `TZ=UTC`, and run the checks and `stat` with the same pinned TZ.

Minor: `report_future.txt` (2035-06-01) stops being future-dated in 2035, which will contradict the hardcoded `report_q3.txt`.

## env_146980 (pygame performance)
(b) **Fixed 10 s wall-clock limit (the known canary failure).** Line 374 `MAX_TOTAL_TIME_SEC = 10.0` applies to `time.perf_counter()` over 500 frames (lines 441-454).
- The reference sits near the author's 7 s target (`performance_targets.json`; 1.5x = 10.5 s), so it has at most about 1.4x headroom when idle. A 2-6x slowdown puts it at roughly 10-40 s.
- CPU generation also shifts the result, because SDL/pygame pick SIMD blitters at runtime.
- Reverse direction: a partial optimisation, such as keeping the six per-layer `self.output.copy()` calls (`compositor.py:65`), passes on an idle host and fails under load.

(c) The original never hangs; it is about 3-4x slower than the target (about 21-28 s). Most of that is 48,000 Python `set_at` calls per frame (`hud.py:52-56`) plus six 3.8 MB surface copies per frame. Fix: use `time.process_time()` and a relative limit. For example, run a pristine copy of the original engine shipped in `/tests` and the agent's engine for about 100 frames each, interleaved, and require the agent's time ≤ 0.5x the original's.

Soundness: the reference HUD cache (`solve.sh:118-120`) blits onto an SRCALPHA bar that is never cleared, so alpha builds up toward 255 frame after frame. The test renders only one frame, so this passes.

## env_164278 (Java dates)
(b) **The reference fails on any UTC+ timezone.**
- `EventParser.java:37` `new SimpleDateFormat("MM/dd/yy")` parses at local midnight in the JVM's default zone, taken from `TZ`.
- `EventProcessor.java:17` and `EventFormatter.java:9,30` format in GMT; the reference leaves the parser as is.
- With `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`, "01/29/02" becomes 2002-01-28 18:30 UTC and prints "28-Jan-2002". Event 3 becomes "30-Nov-2023" with month 11, so the tests at lines 54-59, 98-104 and 112-125 fail and the reference scores 0. UTC and America/* pass.
- Likelihood: certain on UTC+ clusters.
- Fix: `run_tool()` (lines 11-17) should pass `TZ=UTC`.

(d) Locale is not an issue: the reference uses `Locale.ENGLISH`, and the image has no de_DE locale, so Java falls back to en_US. Nine javac+java runs at 60 s each fit comfortably.
